messages:
Jordan: Hey team — quick help needed. Had an emergency dental visit last week. Spouse's employer insurance paid ~60% and provider billed me the remaining balance. I have the provider invoice and the EOB from spouse's insurer. What steps do I take to file a coordination-of-benefits (COB) claim with our plan so I can get reimbursed for the remainder? Do I need a special form or extra info from the spouse's carrier?

Alex (People Ops): Sorry you had to deal with that, Jordan. Short version: yes, we process it as a COB claim. Steps: 1) Download the COB claim form from the benefits portal (Benefits > Claims > Coordination of Benefits). 2) Fill in member details (your Redwood member ID, spouse's insurer name + policy/member ID, date of service, provider NPI if available). 3) Attach the spouse's EOB (PDF) and the provider invoice/statement showing the patient responsibility. 4) Upload via the portal OR email benefits@redwood.com with subject: "COB claim - [Your Name] - [date of service]" if you prefer.

Jordan: Do I need a claim number from the spouse's insurer on the form? Also any tips for provider billing mistakes (they billed spouse instead of me)?

Alex (People Ops): If the spouse's EOB includes their claim ID, put that on the form (helps speed things up). If the provider billed the wrong policy, include a short note and we'll flag it with the carrier — sometimes we can request an adjustment so the patient portion is clearer. Make sure the EOB shows amounts paid and allowed amounts, otherwise processing gets delayed.

Priya: Processing time is usually 7–10 business days after we get everything. If we need more info we'll ping you here or email. If it's urgent, add "EXPEDITE" to the email subject and attach the invoice showing the due date.

BenefitsBot: You can upload documents here: https://benefits.redwood.com/claims/upload :link:

Jordan: Thanks — uploading now. I'll cc spouse's EOB and the invoice. Appreciate the quick guidance. :thumbsup:
